title: Constructing events across perception, action, and thought
title_zh: 构建感知、行动与思维中的事件
abstract: The brain organizes continuous experience into events that structure episodic memory and guide behavior. Traditional accounts have primarily focused on sensory discontinuities and prediction errors that trigger updates of event models. Here, we broaden this view to consider event boundaries arising during goal-directed behavior, spontaneous thought, and memory recall, including transitions generated in the absence of corresponding changes in sensory input. We propose that prediction error and uncertainty provide complementary signals for event model updating: prediction errors signal a violation of current expectations, whereas uncertainty may promote updating when upcoming states become difficult to predict. We further suggest that the hippocampus may serve as a candidate hub linking boundary-related representational changes across perception, action, and thought. Together, this framework offers an integrative account of how the brain detects and generates event structure in continuous experience to support memory and behavior.
abstract_zh: 大脑将连续的经验组织成事件，以构建情景记忆并指导行为。传统的研究主要集中在感官的断裂和触发事件模型更新的预测误差。在此，我们拓宽了这一视角，考虑在目标导向行为、自发思维和回忆过程中产生的事件边界，包括在感官输入无相应变化的情况下产生的转变。我们提出，预测误差和不确定性为事件模型的更新提供互补信号：预测误差表示当前期望的违背，而不确定性可能在即将到来的状态难以预测时促进更新。此外，我们进一步建议，海马体可能作为一个候选枢纽，连接感知、行动和思维中与事件边界相关的表征变化。综上，该框架为大脑如何检测和生成连续经验中的事件结构以支持记忆和行为提供了一个综合性的解释。
